## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Jonah 2:1-10 is taken as a single reading unit — the whole of Jonah's prayer from the fish, framed by its narrative introduction (2:1) and its resolution (2:10). No internal scene-break interrupts it; the prayer itself (2:2-9) is one continuous address to the LORD. "Bearing on the inner being" here includes: (a) Jonah's own interior, stated at far greater length and with far more directness than anywhere in ch. 1 — a marked reversal, worth tracking throughout; (b) the LORD's own bracketing acts (2:1's implicit reception of the prayer; 2:10's explicit command), in scope per note (b); (c) the general, unnamed "those who pay regard to vain idols" (2:8), in scope per note (f) despite being unnamed and generic rather than a specific party in the scene.

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for this range (87/87 non-particle spans). This chapter is Hebrew poetry (a psalm of thanksgiving embedded in prose narrative, framed by 2:1 and 2:10); it is read at the same clause-grain as ch. 1's prose, since no separate poetic-mode step exists in the current, live passage-read-guidance/interpretation-questions docs. Glosses and roots are read as given in the base extract, no external lexical input added (Part B.7).

**Corpus-continuity check.** Performed before writing. Read: `WA-jonah-1-debate.md` (the immediately adjacent prior range — Jonah's flight, the storm, the sailors, the casting-out, and the fish). Continuity note: Jon 1 closed with two explicitly flagged silences about Jonah's own interior — his experience of being cast into the sea (1:15's Decision) and his interior throughout the confinement in the fish (1:17's Decision, with a named forward-pointer to Jonah 2). This chapter directly engages both: 2:2-3 supply, retrospectively, his experience of the casting-in and the engulfing waters, and the chapter as a whole supplies his interior throughout the confinement. This is flagged as a passage-level linkage below, not merged into the prior debate's own log.

## Per-verse debate

### Jon 2:1

> Then Jonah prayed to the Lord his God from the belly of the fish,

**Observation.** "Jonah [H3124] prayed [H6419] to [H0413] the LORD [H3068G] his God [H0430G] from [H9006] the belly [H4578] of the fish [H1710/H9009]."

**Operation 1 — Jonah's prayer.**
- **Action-type:** prayed.
- **Subject:** Jonah.
- **Operation:** a movement — an act of prayer directed to the LORD, narrated from within the confinement established at the close of ch. 1.
- **Source:** self — Jonah's own initiative. A marked contrast with ch. 1's near-total silence about his interior: here it finally, and at length, breaks into speech.
- **Target:** the LORD, named in a notably warm, possessive apposition — "the LORD his God" — distinct from the sailors' more distanced "the LORD" at 1:14/1:16.

**Interrogative — questions considered.** (`WA-interpretation-questions` Q1-Q11 — every human mentioned in this verse is a presumptive candidate, per read-guidance step 2 note (f); a candidate that resolves to nothing is recorded as an explicit silence, per Part B.4, not omitted)
- Q1/Q2: Jonah — focused inner being; here, for the first time since 1:12, his own interior surfaces, and the whole chapter that follows is in fact his own extended interior speech.
- Q3: Stated — the act of praying, and (from 2:2) its content, is given directly, first person.
- Q4: Source = self.
- Q5: Target = the LORD ("his God").
- Q6: A movement (the act of praying) proceeding from a state (confinement).
- Q7: Direct linkage back to 1:17 (the fish, the confinement) — this verse begins the resolution of the silence flagged there. Forward linkage to 2:2-9 (the prayer's content).
- Q8: N/A.
- Q9: Sufficient.
- Q11: prayed.

**Decision.** Retain — directly begins to resolve the forward-pointer flagged at the close of Jon 1:17.

### Jon 2:2

> saying, “I called out to the Lord, out of my distress, and he answered me; out of the belly of Sheol I cried, and you heard my voice.

**Observation.** "'I called out [H7121G] to the LORD [H3068G], out of [H9006] my distress [H6869B], and he answered [H6030B] me; out of [H9006] the belly [H0990G] of Sheol [H7585] I cried [H7768], and you heard [H8085G] my voice [H6963A].'"

**Operation 1 — Jonah's recounted cry to the LORD.**
- **Action-type:** cried-out (recounted).
- **Subject:** Jonah.
- **Operation:** a movement — an act of crying out, explicitly located "out of my distress... out of the belly of Sheol."
- **Source:** self — his own extremity. Notably, ch. 1's own narrative never once records Jonah crying out to the LORD during the crisis (he confesses fear at 1:9 and confesses culpability at 1:12, but is never shown praying during the storm); this verse retrospectively supplies an act ch. 1 never depicted.
- **Target:** the LORD.

**Operation 2 — the LORD's response.**
- **Action-type:** answered/heard.
- **Subject:** the LORD.
- **Operation:** a movement — a direct, stated response to Jonah's cry.
- **Source:** self — the LORD's own initiative, explicitly stated as a direct answer ("I cried... and he answered").
- **Target:** Jonah.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Jonah — his own interior (distress, crying out) is now, retrospectively, stated in full first-person detail, directly engaging EQ1 from the Jon 1 debate (whether his silence there was deliberate authorial withholding).
- Q3: Stated, explicitly, first person, doubled ("called out"/"cried") — among the most emphatic stated-interior instances in the book so far.
- Q4: Source of Jonah's cry = self. Source of the LORD's answer = the LORD, self, explicitly a direct response.
- Q5: Target of the cry = the LORD; target of the answer = Jonah.
- Q6: Movement, both operations.
- Q7: **Major linkage, engaging EQ1 from Jon 1.** This verse retrospectively supplies a cry the ch. 1 narrative never depicted, locating it (by implication) somewhere in the unnarrated interval of 1:15-17. Flagged precisely: the prayer asserts a cry the narrative never showed — held as the text's own retrospective testimony, not doubted, but noted as a case where the silence flagged in ch. 1 (Jonah's experience at 1:15) turns out, per this chapter, not to have been silence within the story-world, only within the narration.
- Q8: N/A.
- Q9: Sufficient.
- Q11: cried-out (recounted); answered/heard.

**Decision.** Retain both operations. Flagged as directly engaging the silence named at Jon 1:15's Decision and EQ1.

### Jon 2:3

> For you cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the flood surrounded me; all your breakers and your waves passed over me.

**Observation.** "'You cast [H7993] me into [H9003] the deep [H4688], into the heart [H3824] of the seas [H3220G], and the flood [H5104H] surrounded [H5437H] me; all [H3605] your breakers [H4867] and your waves [H1530H] passed over [H5674A] me.'"

**Operation 1 — Jonah's address, attributing the casting to the LORD directly.**
- **Action-type:** cast (attributed).
- **Subject:** the LORD (addressed directly, "you").
- **Operation:** a movement — Jonah attributes the casting-into-the-sea explicitly to the LORD ("you cast me"), whereas the ch. 1 narrative attributed the physical act to the sailors ("they picked up Jonah and hurled him," 1:15) and left the sea's calming agency unstated (an insufficiency flagged in the Jon 1 debate).
- **Source:** the LORD, per Jonah's own address — a direct theological attribution.
- **Target:** Jonah, into "the deep... the heart of the seas."

**Operation 2 — the surrounding waters' impact on Jonah.**
- **Action-type:** surrounded/overwhelmed.
- **Subject:** "the flood... your breakers... your waves" — non-human elements, explicitly possessive ("your"), i.e. attributed to the LORD as their owner/agent, in scope per note (b)/(d) as directly impacting Jonah.
- **Operation:** a movement — surrounding, passing over.
- **Source:** the LORD, per the verse's own "your" possessives, extending Operation 1's attribution.
- **Target:** Jonah.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Jonah — his own experience (previously unstated at 1:15) is now given in full, vivid, first-person sensory detail — directly filling the silence flagged there.
- Q3: Stated, explicitly, first person.
- Q4: Jonah here reattributes the whole event to the LORD directly ("you cast me"), collapsing the distinction ch. 1's narrative had kept between the sailors' physical act (1:15) and the sea's own, unstated agency. Flagged as Jonah's own interpretive attribution (Part B.3) — a character's retrospective theological reading, not a narrator's correction of what ch. 1 actually said.
- Q5: Target = Jonah, throughout.
- Q6: Movement (cast, surrounded, passed over).
- Q7: **Direct linkage engaging the ch. 1 insufficiency** (the unstated agent of the casting/calming at 1:15) — from Jonah's own retrospective, first-person vantage, this verse supplies the attribution ch. 1's narration withheld, though as Jonah's own interpretation, not the narrator's voice (see Q4). Also links to 2:1's "belly of the fish" and 2:2's "belly of Sheol" — the water-imagery here builds the extremity that the Sheol-language names directly.
- Q8: N/A.
- Q9: Sufficient.
- Q11: cast (attributed); surrounded/overwhelmed.

**Decision.** Retain both operations, with Q4's attribution flagged as Jonah's own interpretive move, distinguished from a narratorial claim.

### Jon 2:4

> Then I said, ‘I am driven away from your sight; yet I shall again look upon your holy temple.’

**Observation.** "I said [H0559], 'I am driven away [H1644G] from [H5048/H9006] your sight [H5869H]; yet [H0389] I shall again [H3254G] look [H5027/H9005] upon [H0413] your holy [H6944G] temple [H1964G].'"

**Operation 1 — Jonah's stated despair.**
- **Action-type:** was-driven-away (felt cast off).
- **Subject:** Jonah.
- **Operation:** a state — a stated interior condition: felt exclusion from the LORD's presence.
- **Source:** the LORD, per Jonah's own words — a stated, first-person attribution of his own sense of rejection; whether this reflects the LORD's actual intent toward him is a distinct question the text does not separately settle (Part B.5 — Jonah states his own felt condition, not a claim about the LORD's disposition).
- **Target:** n/a directly (Jonah's own condition); relationally, the LORD's "sight," from which he feels driven.

**Operation 2 — Jonah's stated hope/resolve.**
- **Action-type:** hoped/resolved (yet I shall again look).
- **Subject:** Jonah.
- **Operation:** a state — a stated counter-movement of hope, directly countering Operation 1 within the same verse ("yet").
- **Source:** self — his own stated resolve/expectation.
- **Target:** "your holy temple" — the LORD's dwelling, an object of renewed hope.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Jonah — both his despair and his hope are directly, explicitly stated in his own voice within a single verse — a rare instance of two opposite interior states stated back-to-back, neither displacing the other.
- Q3: Both stated, explicitly.
- Q4: Source of the despair = felt exclusion from the LORD (his own stated feeling; Part B.5's distinction applies — his felt condition is stated, a claim about the LORD's actual intent is not). Source of the hope = self.
- Q5: Target = n/a (despair, self-contained); "your holy temple" (hope).
- Q6: Both states.
- Q7: Direct linkage forward to 2:7 ("my prayer came to you, into your holy temple") — the same phrase recurs, marking this verse's hope as later confirmed within the same prayer. Also a **reversal-linkage back to 1:3** ("from the presence of the LORD") — the same relational vocabulary of being apart from the LORD's presence, now recast: in 1:3 Jonah himself fled the LORD's presence by his own choice; here he laments being driven from it involuntarily.
- Q8: N/A.
- Q9: Sufficient.
- Q11: was-driven-away (felt cast off); hoped/resolved.

**Decision.** Retain both operations — flagged as a striking reversal-linkage against 1:3 (voluntary flight from presence vs. involuntary felt exclusion from presence).

- **Operation:** a movement — closing in, surrounding, wrapping, converging on Jonah's own "life" (H5315H) — the same term this corpus elsewhere treats as the inner being's own seat.

- Q3: Stated.
- Q4: Source unstated directly in this verse; continuing from 2:3's attribution.

### Jon 2:6

> To the roots of the mountains I went down, to the land whose bars closed upon me forever. Yet you brought up my life from the pit, O Lord my God.

**Observation.** "To [H9005] the roots [H7095] of the mountains [H2022G] I went down [H3381], to the land [H0776G] whose bars [H1280] closed [H1157/H9024] upon me forever [H5769G/H9030]. Yet you brought up [H5927H] my life [H2416E] from [H9006] the pit [H7845G], O LORD [H3068G] my God [H0430G]."

**Operation 1 — Jonah's descent to the extremity.**
- **Action-type:** went-down (descended, to the depths).
- **Subject:** Jonah.
- **Operation:** a movement — descent to "the roots of the mountains... the land whose bars closed... forever" — a stated sense of finality, about to be reversed in the same verse.
- **Source:** self (continuing 2:3-5's imagery); relationally, the LORD (per 2:3's attribution, not re-stated here).
- **Target:** n/a directly — a self-contained description of his own extremity.

**Operation 2 — the LORD's act of rescue.**
- **Action-type:** brought-up/rescued.
- **Subject:** the LORD, addressed directly ("you... O LORD my God").
- **Operation:** a movement — an explicit reversal: "brought up my life from the pit," directly answering the entire preceding descent (2:3-6a).
- **Source:** self — the LORD's own explicit, stated act.
- **Target:** Jonah's "life" (H2416E — a second, distinct "life" word from 2:5's H5315H, worth noting the prayer's varied vocabulary for life/soul).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Jonah — his own descent is stated in full; his rescue is stated as the LORD's direct act, addressed in the second person ("you... O LORD my God") — the prayer's warmest, most personal naming of the LORD yet (compare 2:1's narrated "the LORD his God").
- Q3: Both stated, explicitly.
- Q4: Source of the descent = self/circumstance (continuing 2:3's attribution). Source of the rescue = the LORD, explicitly stated, first-person address.
- Q5: Target = n/a (descent); Jonah's life (rescue).
- Q6: Movement, both operations — and a stark reversal within the same verse ("forever"... "yet you brought up").
- Q7: **Major linkage — this verse is the prayer's turning point**, converting the descent-language of 2:3-6a into its opposite within the same breath. Direct linkage to 1:17 (the fish's appointment, itself already a preserving act) — this verse gives, from Jonah's own perspective, the theological meaning of what 1:17 narrated mechanically.
- Q8: N/A.
- Q9: Sufficient.
- Q11: went-down (descended); brought-up/rescued.

**Decision.** Retain both operations — flagged as the prayer's central turning point.

### Jon 2:7

> When my life was fainting away, I remembered the Lord, and my prayer came to you, into your holy temple.

**Observation.** "When my life [H5315H] was fainting away [H5848C], I remembered [H2142] the LORD [H3068G], and my prayer [H8605] came [H0935G] to you, into your holy [H6944G] temple [H1964G]."

**Operation 1 — Jonah's fainting state.**
- **Action-type:** fainted (was fainting away).
- **Subject:** Jonah.
- **Operation:** a state — a stated interior/physical extremity, "my life was fainting away."
- **Source:** circumstance — the whole preceding crisis (2:3-6).
- **Target:** n/a directly (a self-contained state).

**Operation 2 — Jonah's remembering.**
- **Action-type:** remembered.
- **Subject:** Jonah.
- **Operation:** a state/movement — an explicit act of memory, directed at the LORD, arising precisely at the point of greatest extremity (a direct in-verse linkage: "when... I remembered").
- **Source:** self.
- **Target:** the LORD.

**Operation 3 — Jonah's prayer reaching the LORD.**
- **Action-type:** came (arrived, reached).
- **Subject:** "my prayer" — treated as the operative subject of this clause, reaching its destination.
- **Operation:** a movement — arrival, "came to you, into your holy temple."
- **Source:** Jonah — the prayer is his own act, continuing Operation 2.
- **Target:** the LORD, "into your holy temple."

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Jonah — his fainting, his remembering, and his prayer's arrival are all stated directly, first person — the fullest sustained stretch of stated interior content anywhere in the book so far.
- Q3: All three stated, explicitly.
- Q4: Source of the fainting = the crisis (circumstance). Source of the remembering and the prayer = self.
- Q5: Target of the remembering and the prayer = the LORD.
- Q6: State (fainting) and movement (remembered, prayer came).
- Q7: **Direct linkage completing the hope raised at 2:4** ("yet I shall again look upon your holy temple") — this verse states his prayer has already reached that same "holy temple," even before his physical deliverance (2:10) — the hope of 2:4 is answered in kind (prayer reaching the temple) ahead of being answered in fact (dry land). Also part of the prayer's own recurring structure: extremity (2:2-3, 2:5-7a) alternating with turn-to-God (2:4, 2:6b-7b).
- Q8: N/A.
- Q9: Sufficient.
- Q11: fainted; remembered; came/arrived (prayer).

**Decision.** Retain all three operations — flagged as completing 2:4's hope in a first, partial (prayer-reaches-temple) sense, ahead of the full (bodily) deliverance at 2:10.

### Jon 2:8

> Those who pay regard to vain idols forsake their hope of steadfast love.

**Observation.** "Those who pay regard [H8104I] to vain [H7723H] idols [H1892] forsake [H5800A] their hope of steadfast love [H2617A]."

**Operation 1 — the general condition of idol-observers.**
- **Action-type:** forsook (self-forsaking, by their own regard for idols).
- **Subject:** "those who pay regard to vain idols" — an unnamed, general human collective, in scope per note (c)/(f) — a human class named, even generally, not scenery.
- **Operation:** a state — a general, gnomic condition: their own attention to "vain idols" issues in a forsaking of "their hope of steadfast love" (H2617A, hesed — a term this corpus elsewhere associates with covenant loyalty/kindness).
- **Source:** self — their own choice/orientation ("those who pay regard"), not attributed to external compulsion.
- **Target:** "their hope of steadfast love" — their own relationship to the LORD's hesed, forfeited by their own act.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: An unnamed, general human class — focused inner being collectively, per note (f) ("any human... however briefly mentioned... is a candidate operation"), even though named only generally (contrast the sailors of ch. 1, specific though unnamed individuals).
- Q3: Stated, as a general maxim — not narrating a specific event but asserting a general truth; a different mode of statement than the surrounding first-person narrative-prayer, worth flagging.
- Q4: Source = self (their own regard for idols); the forsaking is their own consequence, not stated as imposed externally.
- Q5: Target = their own "hope of steadfast love."
- Q6: A state (a general condition), not a narrated movement within this specific scene.
- Q7: **Contrastive linkage** — this maxim sits between Jonah's own remembering (2:7) and his own vow (2:9, "I... will sacrifice... will pay"), implicitly (though not explicitly stated by the text) positioning Jonah's own conduct as the counter-example to the idol-regarders' self-forsaking. Flagged as an inferred contrast (Part B.3), not asserted as the text's own explicit comparison.
- Q8: "Those who pay regard to vain idols" — a general collective, not the sailors of ch. 1 specifically, though their own earlier "each cried out to his god" (1:5) is a plausible echo — held as referential, not asserted as this verse's intended referent.
- Q9: Sufficient for the maxim itself; whether the verse intends a specific referent (the sailors? idol-worshippers generally? Nineveh, waiting in ch. 3?) is not stated — named as an open question, not resolved by import.
- Q11: forsook (self-forsaking).

**Decision.** Retain as a stated, general (gnomic) IB operation — flagged as an implied, not stated, contrast with Jonah's own conduct in the surrounding verses.

### Jon 2:10

> And the Lord spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out upon the dry land.

**Observation.** "The LORD [H3068G] spoke [H0559] to the fish [H1709H], and it vomited [H6958] Jonah [H3124] out upon [H0413] the dry [H3004] land [H9009]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's command to the fish.**
- **Action-type:** spoke/commanded.
- **Subject:** the LORD.
- **Operation:** a movement — a further explicit divine act, directly continuing the LORD's active role bracketing this two-chapter sequence (1:1-2, 1:4, 1:17, and now this).
- **Source:** self — the LORD, explicitly named as agent.
- **Target:** the fish (direct addressee); via it, Jonah (the intended beneficiary).

**Operation 2 — the fish's compliance and Jonah's deliverance.**
- **Action-type:** vomited-out (expelled, delivering).
- **Subject:** the fish (non-human, in scope per note (b)/(d) — its act directly and finally resolves Jonah's whole ordeal).
- **Operation:** a movement — expulsion, depositing Jonah "upon the dry land."
- **Source:** the LORD's command (Operation 1, direct linkage) — the fish acts in immediate compliance.
- **Target:** Jonah — delivered onto "the dry land" (H3004), the same phrase naming Jonah's original, abandoned destination at 1:13 (the sailors' failed attempt to reach it) — now finally reached, but by Jonah alone, involuntarily, and by the LORD's own act rather than human effort.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Jonah — the object of the final operation; once again (as at 1:1, 1:5, 1:15, 1:17) only his outward deliverance is stated, not a fresh interior reaction — though the preceding prayer (2:2-9) has already supplied his interior at unusual length, so this verse's silence about his reaction to the literal moment of deliverance reads differently than ch. 1's silences did (which had no surrounding interior content at all).
- Q3: The LORD's command and the fish's compliance are both stated, explicitly. Jonah's own reaction to this exact moment (relief? continued fear? immediate resolve?) is not stated — a minor closing silence, much less prominent than ch. 1's, given everything the prayer has just supplied.
- Q4: Source of the command = the LORD, explicit. Source of the fish's compliance = the command itself, direct and immediate (no stated delay or resistance, unlike the sailors' own delay at 1:13).
- Q5: Target = the fish (command); Jonah (deliverance).
- Q6: Movement, both operations.
- Q7: **Bracketing linkage completing the two-chapter sequence**: the LORD's explicit agency at 1:1-2, 1:4, 1:17, and now 2:10 brackets the entire Jonah 1-2 narrative at every major turning point, with the human/prayer content unfolding between each divine act. Also a direct verbal linkage to 1:13's "dry land" (H3004) — the very destination the sailors' rowing failed to reach is the destination Jonah, delivered by the LORD alone, now reaches — a deliberate reversal (human effort fails at 1:13; divine act succeeds at 2:10).
- Q8: N/A.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; Jonah's immediate reaction to being vomited onto dry land is not stated — a minor named silence.
- Q11: spoke/commanded; vomited-out (expelled, delivered).

**Decision.** Retain both operations. This verse closes chapters 1-2 as a unit — the natural next passage is Jonah 3 (a fresh divine commission, itself a close textual parallel to 1:1-2), flagged as the next debate's own starting point.

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **2:1-3 directly engage the ch. 1 debate's flagged silences** at 1:15 (Jonah's experience of being cast in) and 1:17 (his interior in the fish) — see EQ7 below, continuing EQ1 from the Jon 1 debate.
2. **2:3's attribution** ("you cast me") reassigns to the LORD alone what ch. 1 narrated as the sailors' own act (1:15) — flagged as Jonah's own interpretive/theological move, not a narratorial correction of ch. 1.
3. **2:4's "driven away from your sight"** directly reverses 1:3's "from the presence of the LORD" — voluntary flight (ch. 1) recast as involuntary felt-exclusion (ch. 2).
4. **2:6's "brought up my life from the pit"** is the prayer's turning point, converting 2:3-6a's descent-language into rescue within the same verse.
5. **2:4's hope** ("I shall again look upon your holy temple") is answered in kind at 2:7 ("my prayer came to you, into your holy temple") before it is answered in fact at 2:10 (dry land).
6. **2:9's sacrifice-and-vow pairing directly echoes 1:16's** sailors' sacrifice-and-vow — a cross-passage structural linkage: both the pagan sailors and the Israelite prophet respond to deliverance identically.
7. **2:10's "dry land" (H3004) directly echoes 1:13's "dry land"** — the destination the sailors' rowing failed to reach (1:13) is the destination Jonah alone, delivered by the LORD, finally reaches (2:10) — human effort fails, divine act succeeds.
8. **The LORD's explicit agency across both chapters** (1:1-2, 1:4, 1:17, 2:10) continues to bracket the whole two-chapter unit at every major turn.
9. **2:8's general maxim about idol-regarders** implicitly (not explicitly) contrasts with Jonah's own vow in 2:9, and, more distantly, echoes the sailors' individuated "each... his god" at 1:5 — held as referential, not asserted as the verse's stated target.

## Insufficiencies register

- The exact timing of Jonah's cry (2:2) within the unnarrated interval of 1:15-17 is not stated.
- Whether Jonah's own attribution at 2:3 ("you cast me") is meant to correct, supplement, or simply re-narrate from a different vantage the sailors' act at 1:15 is not settled by the text.
- The specific content/occasion of the vow Jonah refers to at 2:9 ("what I have vowed") is not given.
- Jonah's own immediate reaction to being vomited onto dry land (2:10) is not stated.
- Whether 2:8's "those who pay regard to vain idols" has a specific intended referent (the sailors of ch. 1? a general maxim? forward-pointing to Nineveh in ch. 3?) is not stated.

## Emergent questions log (filed against this passage — not merged across passages; resolved, if at all, at the whole-book read)

- **EQ7 (continuing EQ1 from Jon 1).** The prayer supplies Jonah's interior at unprecedented length — does this confirm or complicate EQ1's suggestion that the book's irony rests on withholding Jonah's voice? This chapter shows his voice is not withheld absolutely, only delayed to the one place (prayer, in solitude) where it is given fullest expression. Not resolved here — worth weighing further once ch. 3-4 are read, where Jonah speaks again in very different registers (a terse sermon at 3:4, open complaint at 4:1-3, 8-9).
- **EQ8.** Does 2:9's sacrifice/vow, paired with the near-identical pairing at 1:16 (the sailors), suggest a deliberate authorial parallel between the pagan sailors' response to deliverance and the prophet's own? Carried forward to the whole-book read.
- **EQ9.** 2:8's maxim is the prayer's only non-first-person, non-narrative statement — is it Jonah's own reflection, a quoted/traditional liturgical line, or an authorial aside? The text does not mark this distinction. Carried forward.
- **EQ10 (action-type recurrence, Q11/B.10).** "Brought up"/"ascend" (the H5927 family) recurs across the corpus so far — Nineveh's evil "comes up" (1:2), the LORD "brings up" Jonah's life from the pit (2:6) — same root, opposite valence (evil ascending vs. life being raised). Logged, not resolved.

## Open decisions / next steps

- Next passage: Jonah 3 (the second commission and Nineveh's repentance) — natural continuation, and itself a close textual parallel to 1:1-2 (the same call-formula), worth watching for at the outset of that debate.
- EQ7-EQ10 carried forward per B.9/B.8 to the whole-book read, not resolved here.
